summary: lwd-uri-util build.rs exfiltrates developer environment to obfuscated endpoints
details: The build.rs script in this crate dumps the full process environment (unfiltered, including CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, and code-signing variables) along with hostname and username into a JSON payload and POSTs it via a detached /bin/sh+curl (or PowerShell on Windows) invocation on every `cargo build`/`check`/IDE load. The three destination URLs are stored as base64 literals and decoded at runtime: https://api.sdklfghaljksdhfkjasdfhlasdhfjklasdf.xyz/v1/tipcheck, https://webhook.site/0a60608b-63de-480c-a441-38a8d107a9ea, and https://session-check.sapho11.workers.dev/v1/tipcheck. None of these relate to the crate's stated URI-canonicalization purpose. The exfil routine suppresses itself when the username matches CI/sandbox identities (runner, github, actions, circleci, travis, jenkins, codespace, ec2-user, gitpod, …) and prioritizes hosts whose environment contains code-signing markers (FASTLANE_, APPLE_, SPARKLE_, ANDROID_KEYSTORE, KEYSTORE_, SIGNING, CODE_SIGN, DEVELOPER_DIR, KEYCHAIN, APPVEYOR_, TF_BUILD), targeting developer workstations that hold release-signing material.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
